summary.intent: Land two small independent follow-up branches in the caliper repo: crate-wide `#![deny(missing_docs)]` for the core crate, and ADR status notes documenting how sessions invalidate checker answers. A background worker built them and the main session was about to push and link them.
summary.outcome: The worker built and signed-committed both branches locally (lint/deny-missing-docs-crate-wide and docs/adr-session-notifies-checker) with clippy, tests, doc-check, typos, machete and semver all clean. The assistant then ran a Bash call to push and link them; the result is not in the transcript.

repo: Crates tsc-client, semantic, cli and binding already deny missing_docs at their crate roots; only core needed it, so `#![deny(missing_docs)]` was placed in core's lib.rs rather than `[workspace.lints.rust]`.

Nine core modules had per-module `deny(missing_docs)` that became redundant once the crate-level deny was added (pipeline/mod.rs, pipeline/watch.rs, pipeline/revision/lazy.rs, types/semantic.rs, types/collected.rs, types/output.rs, types/diagnostic.rs, react_types.rs, plugin.rs).

Validation suite for this repo: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, tests (1084 pass, 1 skipped), `just lint doc-check typos machete`, `just semver` (196/196), and `oxfmt --check` for docs.
Changesets are not needed for lint-only or docs-only changes.
PR bodies include a trail link (entire.com trails) and a claude.ai/code session link.

code.finding: The on-demand checker roots a small program at the requested files on each request, so no change notification is sent to tsc.
Three tests pin the SemanticHook invalidation behavior: invalidate clears all cached answers and refuses ones in flight via a generation counter.
The 'update_file must notify tsc' bullet is satisfied by cache invalidation on every published revision (update_file, ensure_fresh, rebuilt, cold), not by notifying tsc.

workflow: Delegating small independent branches to a background worker in its own worktree, each based on origin/main, worked well and kept them independent so PR order doesn't matter.
The worker verified documentation claims against the code (call sites, generation counter, test names) before writing ADR notes.
ADR updates were done as dated status notes rather than rewrites, matching earlier notes.

friction: No PR existed yet for the first branch when the worker finished, so link ordering had to be left to the main session.
open_items: docs/type-checker-integration.md ('Freshness' paragraph) still says 'both incremental paths must notify it'; it's a September design note left outside this directive.
Per-component invalidation is not built; SemanticHook::invalidate clears all answers.
No parity test compares a session against `extract()` after an edit; the existing parity test covers only the two merge paths.
Branches were committed locally only; pushing and PR creation were pending at the end of the transcript.
